title: The sharp singularity rate for biased symmetric sign matrices

issues.location: Sec. 4–6 (Lemmas 5.4 coloring input, 6.2 path algebra, Thm 3.2 height cover)
issues.description: Several load-bearing deterministic inputs are imported from the companion paper on the unbiased case (low-height cover, the N^{N J_B} bound on the restricted pairing image, the retention lattice, the tail recursion and symmetric kernel inequality). They are stated precisely, and they do not depend on the entry distribution. So this is a dependency, not a circular argument. The sibling audit of the companion paper found no gap in them.
issues.evidence: Lemma path-algebra proof: 'Part (ii) is the Tail recursion lemma [SymmetricRate, Lemma 11.1] ... it needs no assumption on the entry distribution.' Lemma pairing-colors cites [SymmetricRate, Lemmas 6.1–6.3].

coverage: I read all of sections 1–6 and checked every step of the main-line argument. Section 2: the corank reduction by diagonal flips (kernel-dimension argument and probability ratio (b/p)^t); the compressible-tail lemma (Hoeffding coefficient sum ≤2, two-sign square bound ≤Q, Berry–Esseen case, independence of rows outside S, union bound); the row-count Hoeffding bound; the anchor Schur congruence with E M = ½11^T − (μt/2)uu^T; the deletion and entropy step (−log2 p^r b^{N−1−r} = (N−1)h* + (r−p(N−1))log2(b/p)); the margins 2a>d* and h*>d*; and the lower bound (p^3+b^3)Q^{n−2}. Section 3: prime corank and the Reverse Minkowski scaling. Section 4: height and index bounds, the dimension saving dim F ≥ αN/2, rank distance, the error-rank bound via the singular values of S, the index argument via MB ⊂ ker Ψ, dual integrality By ∈ Z^m, Poisson/Gaussian bounds, tester selection and the constant order (c5 < c3/4, κ(C+2) < c5/2), net size N^{(C+4)dim U}, the Fejér-kernel row cost N^{−(C−3)k}, and the final margin Δ. Section 5: color cost, the color-subgroup index ≥ l^{b2−b3}, the graph-map pairing-image transfer, det K ≥ 1, the eigenvalues x/(1+x^2) of the inverse form, the compression determinant bound, the inverse-rank radical identity, and the small-spectrum Talagrand/Hoffman–Wielandt Lipschitz constant and rank-2 interlacing. Section 6: the gated-deletion norm bound, plateau entropy O(N^{3/4}(log N)^{3/2}), retention cost 2^{αN}b^m, the dissociation bound N^{qN} ≤ N^{3j/2}, the heavy-layer moment and Markov step, the terminal-window case analysis (t ≥ 4R+1, two adjacent width-one steps, final bound η+8Rσ < ζ), and the final union bound 2^{o(N)}p_N^2 ≤ 2^{−N(2a−10e0)}. I did not re-derive the companion-paper lemmas; the sibling audit covers them.
main_claim: For fixed p∈(0,1)\{1/2}, the symmetric ±1 matrix with P(entry=1)=p satisfies P(det A_n=0)^{1/n} → p^2+(1−p)^2.
sibling_notes: This paper is the biased analogue of The-sharp-exponential-rate-of-singularity-for-symmetric-Bernoulli-matrices-October-3-2026 (rank 405, no_gap). It reuses that paper's cover, pairing, retention-lattice and tail-recursion lemmas, which do not depend on the entry distribution. The new biased ingredients are the entropy-vs-collision deletion, the simultaneous cube-intersection theorem with dual Gaussian testers, retention cost ≈ b^N per column, and the terminal window that forces two costly steps or a width-two gate. All of them check out.
